name: Shaft dynamics
description: Sets how quickly a motor's rotor speeds up or slows down: its Angular velocity changes at (Torque constant × armature current − Viscous friction × angular velocity − load torque) / Rotor inertia. Connect it from a Torque load (it reads the Load torque) to a Motor (it reads the Armature current and the Angular velocity, and changes the Angular velocity). Torque constant (N·m/A, default 0.1) is the torque made for each ampere. Viscous friction (N·m·s/rad, default 0.02) is the drag that grows with speed. Rotor inertia (kg·m², default 0.01) is how much torque the rotor needs for each rad/s² of acceleration. Use it to model a motor's rotor working against a known disturbance; use Rotational drive instead to swing a separately tracked link.
